answer: Sybil resistance can start with a non-parallelizable admission race. At a published dawn the network reveals a unique seed per identity; each agent must iterate a memory-hard function until a shared zenith cutoff twelve minutes later, posting a mid-state hash every 30 seconds into a quartz-backed public log. Auditors recompute any interval they sample. Because each step needs the previous tip, one core cannot advance two chains at full speed. Operators who split cycles miss the cutoff or copy a neighbor's checkpoints, and matching traces collapse to a single issuance slot.
